subsystems.name: Target discovery
subsystems.role: finds genes where a change causally shifts the rate of ageing, rather than merely correlating with it.
parts: human genetics of long-lived families and rare variants
genome-wide CRISPR screens in cells and organoids

subsystems.name: Editing machinery
subsystems.role: makes the intended DNA change with as few unintended ones as possible.
parts: Cas9 nickase or base editors that avoid double-strand breaks
prime editors for insertions and small rewrites

subsystems.name: Delivery
subsystems.role: gets the editor into the right organ and cell type, and nowhere else.

subsystems.name: Durability and control
subsystems.role: editing is permanent, so the dose cannot be adjusted later.

subsystems.name: Safety and immunology
subsystems.role: detects off-target edits and manages immune reactions to the editing proteins.

subsystems.name: Outcome measurement
subsystems.role: replaces 'lifespan' with endpoints a trial can actually measure.
parts: epigenetic clocks and other ageing biomarkers

buildSteps.title: Find a causal target
buildSteps.detail: Search human genetics and CRISPR screens for variants that change disease risk or ageing pace, then confirm the effect by editing the gene in human cells and organoids.

buildSteps.title: Design the editor
buildSteps.detail: Choose the smallest effective change — often a single base — and pick an editor that introduces no double-strand break, since breaks invite rearrangements.

buildSteps.title: Validate in cells
buildSteps.detail: Measure on-target efficiency, then sequence the whole genome to count off-target edits before anything enters an animal.

buildSteps.title: Choose a delivery route
buildSteps.detail: Lipid nanoparticles suit the liver; other organs need engineered viral vectors or new chemistries, tested for where they actually end up.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Premature-ageing and naturally ageing mice are dosed and followed for healthspan and lifespan, with tissues examined for tumours.

buildSteps.title: Run safety studies
buildSteps.detail: Long-term dosing studies check immune reactions, organ damage and any sign of cancer before a regulator will allow a human dose.

buildSteps.title: Trial in a severe single-gene disease first
buildSteps.detail: The first plausible use is a rare premature-ageing disorder such as Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome, where the cause is one mutation and the benefit is clear.

buildSteps.title: Extend to age-related disease
buildSteps.detail: If safe, the same machinery is aimed at a common condition driven partly by one gene — for example, permanently lowering cholesterol by editing a liver gene.

buildSteps.title: Only then attempt rate-of-ageing
buildSteps.detail: Any attempt to slow ageing itself would combine several targets at once, guided by biomarkers rather than lifespan, which no trial can measure in reasonable time.

prerequisites.tech: Precise editors with minimal off-target effects
prerequisites.why: base and prime editors avoid double-strand breaks, but off-target edits still occur and are hard to rule out completely.

prerequisites.tech: Delivery to organs beyond the liver
prerequisites.why: lipid nanoparticles reach the liver well; heart, muscle, brain and fat — where ageing acts — remain difficult.
ageing is polygenic and no single edit is known to lengthen human life.
a permanent edit given to healthy people must be near-zero-risk, and decades of follow-up do not yet exist.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory and trial endpoints for ageing
prerequisites.why: regulators do not approve treatments for ageing as such, only for specific diseases.

pathway.milestone: the first CRISPR therapy was approved in 2023 for sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassaemia
pathway.unlocks: proof that a permanent edit can safely correct a human disease outside the body.

pathway.milestone: in-body editing trials for common conditions such as high cholesterol
pathway.unlocks: evidence that editors can be delivered safely inside patients, not just in a laboratory dish.
the first safety and biomarker data linking a genetic edit to ageing biology in people.

pathway.milestone: combination edits guided by ageing biomarkers
pathway.unlocks: a possible slowing of age-related decline — speculative, and dependent on solving delivery and safety first.
